prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Labour’s 2015 manifesto argues Britain can be better by rebuilding a country that works for working people, not just a privileged few. Its core test is simple: Britain only succeeds when working families succeed. That means responsible finances, fair rules, strong public services, decent work and wages, power closer to communities, and an outward-looking nation.

Budget Responsibility Lock
- Every pledge fully funded with no additional borrowing; deficit cut every year; debt falling and a current budget surplus as soon as possible, independently verified by the OBR and with parties’ manifestos audited.
- Fair taxes: restore the 50p rate over £150,000; introduce a 10p starting rate; no rises in basic or higher Income Tax, National Insurance or VAT; abolish non-dom status; close avoidance and loopholes.

An economy that rewards work
- Raise the National Minimum Wage to over £8 by Oct 2019; promote the Living Wage via procurement and “Make Work Pay” tax rebates.
- Ban exploitative zero‑hours contracts; end agency undercutting; scrap employment tribunal fees.
- Back small firms: cut and freeze business rates; create a British Investment Bank and regional banks; keep the most competitive G7 corporation tax rate.
- A long-term industrial strategy: a National Infrastructure Commission; HS2 with cost control and better northern rail; high-speed broadband nationwide; green leadership with a 2030 decarbonised power target, empowered Green Investment Bank, and a million green jobs.
- Fix broken markets: freeze energy bills to 2017 and reform the energy market; boost home energy efficiency; water affordability scheme; rail reform with a public operator option, fare freeze then strict caps, and integrated local bus powers.

Opportunities for the next generation
- Cut university tuition fees to £6,000; tackle unpaid internships.
- Guarantee an apprenticeship for every school leaver with the grades; create Technical Degrees; Youth Allowance linked to training.
- Protect the whole education budget; all teachers qualified; cap infant class sizes; new Technical Baccalaureate; stronger local school standards oversight.

Stronger families, homes and care
- Expand free childcare to 25 hours for working parents of 3–4 year‑olds; wraparound care 8am–6pm; double paternity leave and pay.
- Build at least 200,000 homes a year by 2020; first call for local first-time buyers; “use it or lose it” powers on land; new garden cities; three‑year tenancies with rent rise ceilings; ban letting fees; landlord register; abolish the Bedroom Tax; tackle homelessness.

Rescue and renew the NHS
- 20,000 more nurses, 8,000 more GPs, 3,000 more midwives funded by a mansion tax on £2m+ properties, a tobacco levy, and anti‑avoidance.
- 48‑hour GP appointments; one‑week cancer tests; integrate physical, mental and social care; parity for mental health; 5,000 new home‑care workers; end 15‑minute visits; repeal the Coalition’s NHS marketisation and cap private profits.

Safe, fair and welcoming communities
- 1,000 extra border staff; two‑year wait for EU migrants to claim benefits; English requirement in public‑facing services; crack down on labour exploitation and rogue agencies; humane enforcement ending indefinite detention for vulnerable people.
- Protect neighbourhood policing by safeguarding over 10,000 officers; a Victims’ Law; tougher action on extremism and hate crime.

Power closer to people and a better politics
- English Devolution Act transferring £30bn to city and county regions; votes at 16; a people‑led Constitutional Convention; replace the Lords with a Senate of the Nations and Regions; stronger transparency and lobbying rules; gender pay gap reporting; implement Leveson.

Britain in the world
- Stay in and reform the EU; no transfer of powers without an in/out referendum lock.
- Strong NATO commitment; Strategic Defence and Security Review; maintain a minimum, credible independent nuclear deterrent while pursuing multilateral disarmament.
- Lead on climate with a global net‑zero goal in the second half of the century; uphold 0.7% aid; champion human rights, including new envoys for Religious Freedom and LGBT rights.

The offer: live within our means, make fair choices, and ensure everyone plays by the same rules—so Britain works again for working people.
